speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; can you tell me if the rash appeared immediately after birth or developed a few days later, and does it look like small blisters or a flat redness?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the rash appeared just yesterday in a term infant with a maternal history of gonorrhea, is there any discharge from the eyes or ears, and does the baby seem feverish or lethargic? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and Blood Culture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pneumonia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Dermatitis. The combination of a generalized pustular rash on a 4-day-old with a maternal history of gonorrhea, despite prior treatment years ago, is classic for this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Lesions_Close_Up.
